subject: FY26 Preliminary Budget Review and Software Modernization
overview: The committee held its first preliminary budget hearing for fiscal year 2026, focusing on the city's general fiscal outlook and the budgets for Finance and the Council on Aging. Members discussed a projected deficit driven by rising fixed costs and requested a formal plan for transitioning from legacy financial software to a modern system.

items.title: Fiscal Year 2026 Budget Outlook
items.summary: Chief of Staff Nina Nazarian reported a preliminary $1 million deficit for the $200 million FY 2026 budget, noting that rising health insurance, waste management, and contractual costs are outpacing revenue growth. The administration indicated that the recent property tax override prevents significant municipal and school service cuts despite these pressures.

items.title: Finance and Procurement
items.summary: The committee reviewed the $881,351 budget request and discussed the substantial limitations and hidden labor costs of the city's current paper-based financial systems. A motion was approved requesting a report by September 30 on the implementation costs and training logistics required to transition the city to a modern, integrated financial software suite.

items.title: Council on Aging
items.summary: Director Pam Kelly presented a largely flat-funded $280,064 personnel budget and explained that approximately $200,000 in additional senior programming is supported through state formula grants and federal funds. The committee discussed the success of monthly listening sessions held for seniors who cannot easily visit City Hall.
